findings.title: Lightness value swapped introduces unintended color change for light theme
findings.body: In `.embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a`, the color was previously `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The new code is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`. Following the pattern used everywhere else in this PR, the first (light-theme) argument should preserve the original 30% lightness value (paired with secondary at 70%), i.e. `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, 30%), scale-color($secondary, 70%))`. Instead the primary lightness was changed to 70%, which changes the rendered color in the default/light theme (previously a darker 30%-lightness shade, now a much lighter 70%-lightness shade) — an unintended visual regression unrelated to the PR's stated purpose of only adding dark-theme support.

findings.title: Lightness value changed (30% -> 50%) in .group-member-info .name, altering light-theme appearance
findings.body: `.user-stream .group-member-info .name` previously used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The new code is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. To preserve the original light-theme look (consistent with the sibling `.title` rule which kept 50%/50% because it was originally 50%), this should have been `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, 30%), scale-color($secondary, 70%))`. As written, the light theme's text color for this element changes from a darker 30%-lightness shade to a lighter 50%-lightness shade, which is an unrelated visual regression.

findings.title: Lightness values swapped for .custom-message-length, darkening text in light theme
findings.body: `.custom-message-length` previously used `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`. The replacement is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. The light-theme (first) argument should retain the original 70% lightness (paired with 30% for secondary/dark-theme), i.e. `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, 70%), scale-color($secondary, 30%))`. As written, the light theme now renders this text with a much darker (30%) shade instead of the original lighter (70%) shade — a visual regression unrelated to dark-theme support.

findings.title: Lightness value changed (20% -> 50%) for .topic-map h3, altering light-theme heading color
findings.body: `.topic-map h3` previously used `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)`. The new code is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The sibling `.map .number, i` rule in the same file correctly kept its original 20% value and used 80% for the counterpart (`dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, 20%), scale-color($secondary, 80%))`), showing the intended pattern. This h3 rule instead was changed to 50%/50%, meaning the light theme's heading color shifts from a dark 20%-lightness shade to a medium 50%-lightness shade, an unintended visual regression.

findings.title: Lightness value changed (30% -> 50%) in .group-member-info .name, altering light-theme appearance (duplicate of desktop/user.scss issue)
findings.body: `.user-stream .group-member-info .name` previously used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The new code is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))` instead of the expected `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, 30%), scale-color($secondary, 70%))`. This duplicates the same regression found in the desktop variant of this stylesheet: the light theme's text color changes from darker 30%-lightness to lighter 50%-lightness, an unintended side effect beyond the PR's stated scope.

findings.title: Missed conversion: .topic-list.categories .category .badge-notification color still uses raw scale-color($primary) without a dark-theme fallback
findings.body: In `.topic-list.categories .category .badge-notification`, `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%);` was left unconverted, while every other occurrence of `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)` in this same file (e.g. the `th`, `td`, `.topic-excerpt`, and `div.education` rules a few lines above/below) was updated to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, 50%), scale-color($secondary, 50%))`. Because this instance was missed, the badge-notification text color inside category topic lists will still be computed purely from `$primary` and will not adapt for dark themes, defeating the purpose of this PR for this specific element and likely resulting in poor contrast/readability in dark themes.
